newsitem.title: PERU: Suspected rebels kill Peruvian policeman.
newsitem.headline: Suspected rebels kill Peruvian policeman.

text.p: Suspected leftist guerrillas shot dead one policeman and injured another on Tuesday night while the pair was patrolling a Lima suburb, police said.
The shooting, at about 10 p.m. (0300 GMT Wednesday), coincided with the detonation of small explosives at a Lima cinema on Tuesday.

Police believe the attacks to be the work of the Shining Path guerrilla movement, which last week set off a powerful car bomb in what was seen as the start of a new offensive. Ten people were injured in last week's attack.

The smaller Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), who overshadowed the Shining Path with a four-month siege of the Japanese ambassador's residence, has also threatened reprisal attacks against security forces.
Peruvian troops killed 14 MRTA rebels during an April 22 operation to release their 72 hostages, who had been held at the residence since Dec. 17.
Two soldiers and one of the hostages also died in the bloody finale to the crisis.
